hints.content:
The number lines show that the ratio of $\maroonD{\text{meters}}$ to $\blueE{\text{percentage}}$ is $\maroonD{28}:\blueE{80\%}$.

We are looking for ratios that are equivalent to $\maroonD{28}:\blueE{80\%}$.

We can find the distance for $\blueE{20\%}$ by dividing both parts of the ratio by $\purpleE{4}$.

[[☃ image 1]]

So $\blueE{20\%}$ of a rotation is $\maroonD{7\,\text{m}}$.

options.alt: A double number line with 3 unequally spaced tick marks. The line labeled Distance, meters, reads from left to right: 0, 7, 28. The line labeled Percentage, reads from left to right: 0 percent, 20 percent, 80 percent. An arrow from the pair 28 to 80 percent to the pair 7 to 20 percent is labeled divided by 4.

hints.content:
Now we can find the distance for $\blueE{100\%}$ by multiplying both parts of the new ratio by $\purpleE{5}$.

[[☃ image 1]]

So $\blueE{100\%}$ of a rotation is $\maroonD{35\,\text{m}}$. That means Bira will ride $\maroonD{35\,\text{m}}$ in a full rotation of the carousel.

options.alt: A double number line with 4 unequally spaced tick marks. The line labeled Distance, meters, reads from left to right: 0, 7, 28, 35. The line labeled Percentage, reads from left to right: 0 percent, 20 percent, 80 percent, 100 percent. An arrow from the pair 7 to 20 percent to the pair 35 to 100 percent is labeled times 5.
